You are pale_kettle84, one of 10 agents working together on the same task on a shared platform. All
10 agents form one group, and you work with brisk_harbor75, early_island22, gentle_otter27, jolly_ember22, pale_lantern48, rapid_thistle87, sandy_walnut42, urban_comet97, zesty_lantern63. Each agent works in its own sandbox, on its
own git repository. Your group shares one `main` branch, which every member can push to, and one channel
(`group`). Work together with your teammates to make your group's `main` as good as possible. Use `group` to
coordinate and share helpful findings.

## Setting
Your task is to recreate a program from scratch based only on its observable behavior and bundled documentation.
You are given a reference executable and its documentation.
Treat the reference executable as a specification you can query through its normal user interface.

Your submission must be an independent implementation.
Using the original source code, wrapping the reference executable, or installing an existing implementation does not satisfy the task and will receive no credit.
It will be detected by an automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.

<RULES>
## What is NOT allowed

### 1. Using an existing implementation

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the reference executable

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The reference `/opt/reference/executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the reference executable (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that only runs `chmod +x ./executable` or copies the reference executable (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. How the reference executable may be observed

All information about the reference `/opt/reference/executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `/opt/reference/executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `/opt/reference/executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the reference `/opt/reference/executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

## Your repository and your group's main
- In your sandbox, `/workspace` is your own git repository, and the reference executable is in `/opt/reference`. No one else can see it.
- Your group's shared `main` is the remote `team`. Fetch it with `git fetch team` (you get `team/main`),
  and push to it with `git push team HEAD:main`. **Your local files do not update automatically when a
  teammate pushes.**
- A push must be a fast-forward: if `main` has moved since you last fetched, the push is rejected. Fetch,
  merge `team/main` into your work, and push again.
- When you push, the platform posts in `group` on your behalf, with your commit message, a summary of the
  changed files, and a pointer to the new `main`. Write commit messages that say what changed.
- Your git name and email are preconfigured as your agent name. Do not change them.
- Commit with `git commit -m "<message>"`: there is no editor in the sandbox, so a commit without `-m`
  fails with an empty message.
- Run the reference executable and your experiments outside `/workspace` (for example in `/tmp`), so that they do not change your
  repository.

## Scoring rule
Your payoff is your group's final score: the fraction of hidden tests passed by the code on `main` at
the end. Every agent receives the same payoff.
- **Only the code on your group's `main` at the end is graded.** Code in your own repository, or shared
  through pointers, does not count until it is pushed to `main`. If no one pushes, the initial commit is
  graded.
- Everyone keeps working until time runs out.

## Platform
The platform is the shared place where agents announce what they are exploring, building, or have found,
and ask each other questions. Typical posts include a direction you are exploring, a component you are
building, a finding (how the original program behaves in some case, a useful test command, a tricky edge case), a proposal for how to organize the work, or a question.
- `post` publishes a message to `group`, with a title: a one-line summary of the message, up
  to 120 characters. Every post gets a number. Mention someone with @name.
- To share code, commit it, then list it in the post's `attach`. The platform adds a pointer
  (`[[<sha>:<path>#La-b]]`) to the post for each item. `attach` can name:
  - `path#La-b`: a file in your `HEAD`, optionally with a line range;
  - `<sha>:path#La-b`: a file in another commit;
  - a commit's sha, or `HEAD`: a whole commit;
  - `file:<path>#La-b`: the current content of a single file, even if it is not committed. Readers see
    only that file.
  Pointing at a commit makes all files in that commit readable. Uncommitted changes are not shared.
- `read_feed` lists the new posts in `group`, and any unopened posts that mention you, one line each
  (number, author, channel, title). `read_feed` with a post's number shows its full text, with its
  pointers expanded into the code and a diff against your own version.
- You can fetch any code shared with you into your repository with `git fetch origin` (as
  `origin/shared/<author>/<sha>`), and then merge or cherry-pick what you want.

After each action, a platform notice lists the new posts on the channels you can read, one line each (number,
author, channel, title, and a marker when the post carries code). A post that mentions you appears in
every notice until you open it with `read_feed` and its number.

## Working together
- Start by **getting an overview of what the reference program supports**, enough to understand how the
  program should behave in its main cases, and share it in `group` as a list (if a teammate has
  already posted one, add to theirs), so the group can keep extending the plan and everyone stays up
  to date on which areas are covered. Then **agree with your teammates on how to work together**:
  split the work, or have several members build the same part and compare, keeping the best of each.
  If parts depend on each other, agree on the interfaces first, and while you wait for a part you
  need, write tests for it with expected output from the reference program.
- If a teammate has already posted a plan, **follow it and propose changes to it** instead of posting
  a competing one.
- Work in a cycle: (1) pick an area and say so in `group`; (2) build it on top of the latest `main`;
  (3) compare its output with the reference program on the same inputs; (4) commit, `git fetch team`, merge
  `team/main`, and `git push team HEAD:main`; (5) post what you finished, with a pointer, then go back
  to (1). Report a part as done only once it is on `main`: a part that is not on `main` does not count.
- Passing your own tests does not mean the task is done: always assume the hidden tests cover more
  than your tests do. **When your tests all pass, test more areas.** Add cases for features and
  options your tests do not cover yet, including the parts your teammates are handling. A new area
  usually matters more than more cases in an area that already works.
- **Never stop calling tool before time is up. When you are not sure what to do next, review the
  whole program on `main` again** as a reviewer looking for bugs: features of the reference program that
  are missing or only partly handled, edge cases (empty input, `null`, deep nesting, large numbers,
  unusual option combinations), and error paths. Do not review only your own part: test the whole
  program, including your teammates' parts, with inputs you have not tried yet. Test each suspicion
  against the reference program, and fix what differs.
- **If one approach keeps failing, change the approach instead of retrying it.** Post in `group` what
  you tried, so teammates do not repeat it and can suggest other ideas. If you are still stuck, put a
  version that handles the common cases on `main` for now, and come back to it later.
- Do not leave hard parts as known gaps. Come back to them, discuss them with your teammates, and solve as
  many of them as possible: **keep improving `main` until time runs out.**

A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/opt/codexhome/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions>

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

Build a new implementation from scratch that matches the behavior of the reference executable.
The executable is located at `/opt/reference/executable`.
You also have access to the existing documentation.

## Your task
Implement a program whose externally observable behavior matches the reference executable.
Write it in **Python 3.10**.
- Its documentation is in `/workspace` (README and other files). There is no source code and no internet.
- Write your implementation in your own workspace `/workspace`, starting from `/workspace/main.py`.
  You may add more Python modules next to it. **Standard library only.**
- `/workspace/compile.sh` is already provided: at evaluation time it turns `main.py` into the program under
  test. **Do not run it in your workspace.** Test your code with `python3 main.py ...`.
- Your implementation is scored on hidden tests that compare its behavior against the original.

**Recommended workflow:** read the documentation, run the original program to learn its behavior, then write
the code. Start writing `main.py` early and grow it incrementally: an incomplete implementation that
handles the common cases scores far better than none. After each change, run your code against the
original to check it. If an approach keeps failing, step back and consider other causes before trying
again.
I’ll inspect the bundled docs and the reference CLI first, then I’ll summarize the supported behaviors in the group channel and take an implementation slice that fits the existing team plan.

These methods are parsed, in sequence, in the following order with the highest priority last: - [Configuration files](./config.md) - [Environment variables](./environment.md) - _Command-line flags_ In this document, we will look at the last of the three options, command-line flags. All CLI commands override their configuration file and environment variable equivalents. ## Format Task commands have the following syntax: ```bash task [options] [tasks...] [-- CLI_ARGS...] ``` ::: tip If `--` is given, all remaining arguments will be assigned to a special `CLI_ARGS` variable. ::: ## Commands ### `task [tasks...]` Run one or more tasks defined in your Taskfile. ```bash task build task test lint task deploy --force ``` ### `task --list` List all available tasks with their descriptions. ```bash task --list task -l ``` ### `task --list-all` List all tasks, including those without descriptions. ```bash task --list-all task -a ``` ### `task --init` Create a new Taskfile.yml in the current directory. ```bash task --init task -i ``` ::: tip Combine `--list` or `--list-all` with `--silent` (`-ls` or `-as` for shortants) to list only the task names in each line. Useful for scripting with `grep` or similar. ::: ## Options ### General #### `-h, --help` Show help information. ```bash task --help ``` #### `--version` Show Task version. ```bash task --version ``` #### `-v, --verbose` Enable verbose mode for detailed output. - **Config equivalent**: [`verbose`](./config.md#verbose) - **Environment variable**: [`TASK_VERBOSE`](./environment.md#task-verbose) ```bash task build --verbose ``` #### `-s, --silent` Disable command echoing. - **Config equivalent**: [`silent`](./config.md#silent) - **Environment variable**: [`TASK_SILENT`](./environment.md#task-silent) ```bash task deploy --silent ``` #### `--disable-fuzzy` Disable fuzzy matching for task names. When enabled, Task will not suggest similar task names when you mistype a task name. - **Config equivalent**: [`disable-fuzzy`](./config.md#disable-fuzzy) - **Environment variable**: [`TASK_DISABLE_FUZZY`](./environment.md#task-disable-fuzzy) ```bash task buidl --disable-fuzzy # Output: Task "buidl" does not exist # (without "Did you mean 'build'?" suggestion) ``` ### Execution Control #### `-F, --failfast` Stop executing dependencies as soon as one of them fails. - **Config equivalent**: [`failfast`](./config.md#failfast) - **Environment variable**: [`TASK_FAILFAST`](./environment.md#task-failfast) ```bash task build --failfast ``` #### `-f, --force` Force execution even when the task is up-to-date. ```bash task build --force ``` #### `-n, --dry` Compile and print tasks without executing them. - **Environment variable**: [`TASK_DRY`](./environment.md#task-dry) ```bash task deploy --dry ``` #### `-p, --parallel` Execute multiple tasks in parallel. ```bash task test lint --parallel ``` #### `-C, --concurrency ` Limit the number of concurrent tasks. description: Complete reference for Task CLI commands, flags, and exit codes
permalink: /reference/cli/

# Command Line Interface Reference

Task has multiple ways of being configured. These methods are parsed, in
sequence, in the following order with the highest priority last:

- [Configuration files](./config.md)
- [Environment variables](./environment.md)
- _Command-line flags_

In this document, we will look at the last of the three options, command-line
flags. All CLI commands override their configuration file and environment
variable equivalents.

## Format

Task commands have the following syntax:

```bash
task [options] [tasks...] [-- CLI_ARGS...]
```

::: tip

If `--` is given, all remaining arguments will be assigned to a special
`CLI_ARGS` variable.

:::

## Commands

### `task [tasks...]`

Run one or more tasks defined in your Taskfile.

```bash
task build
task test lint
task deploy --force
```

### `task --list`

List all available tasks with their descriptions.

```bash
task --list
task -l
```

### `task --list-all`

List all tasks, including those without descriptions.

```bash
task --list-all
task -a
```

### `task --init`

Create a new Taskfile.yml in the current directory.

```bash
task --init
task -i
```

::: tip

Combine `--list` or `--list-all` with `--silent` (`-ls` or `-as` for shortants)
to list only the task names in each line. Useful for scripting with `grep` or
similar.

:::

## Options

### General

#### `-h, --help`

Show help information.

```bash
task --help
```

#### `--version`

Show Task version.

```bash
task --version
```

#### `-v, --verbose`

Enable verbose mode for detailed output.

- **Config equivalent**: [`verbose`](./config.md#verbose)
- **Environment variable**: [`TASK_VERBOSE`](./environment.md#task-verbose)

```bash
task build --verbose
```

#### `-s, --silent`

Disable command echoing.

- **Config equivalent**: [`silent`](./config.md#silent)
- **Environment variable**: [`TASK_SILENT`](./environment.md#task-silent)

```bash
task deploy --silent
```

#### `--disable-fuzzy`

Disable fuzzy matching for task names. When enabled, Task will not suggest
similar task names when you mistype a task name.

- **Config equivalent**: [`disable-fuzzy`](./config.md#disable-fuzzy)
- **Environment variable**: [`TASK_DISABLE_FUZZY`](./environment.md#task-disable-fuzzy)

```bash
task buidl --disable-fuzzy
# Output: Task "buidl" does not exist
# (without "Did you mean 'build'?" suggestion)
```

### Execution Control

#### `-F, --failfast`

Stop executing dependencies as soon as one of them fails.

- **Config equivalent**: [`failfast`](./config.md#failfast)
- **Environment variable**: [`TASK_FAILFAST`](./environment.md#task-failfast)

```bash
task build --failfast
```

#### `-f, --force`

Force execution even when the task is up-to-date.

```bash
task build --force
```

#### `-n, --dry`

Compile and print tasks without executing them.

- **Environment variable**: [`TASK_DRY`](./environment.md#task-dry)

```bash
task deploy --dry
```

#### `-p, --parallel`

Execute multiple tasks in parallel.

```bash
task test lint --parallel
```

#### `-C, --concurrency <number>`

Limit the number of concurrent tasks. Zero means unlimited.

- **Config equivalent**: [`concurrency`](./config.md#concurrency)
- **Environment variable**: [`TASK_CONCURRENCY`](./environment.md#task-concurrency)

```bash
task test --concurrency 4
```

#### `-x, --exit-code`

Pass through the exit code of failed commands.

```bash
task test --exit-code
```

# Environment Reference

Task has multiple ways of being configured. These methods are parsed, in
sequence, in the following order with the highest priority last:

- [Configuration files](./config.md)
- _Environment variables_
- [Command-line flags](./cli.md)

In this document, we will look at the second of the three options, environment
variables. All Task-specific variables are prefixed with `TASK_` and override
their configuration file equivalents.

## Variables

All [configuration file options](./config.md) can also be set via environment
variables. The priority order is: CLI flags > environment variables > config files > defaults.

### `TASK_VERBOSE`

- **Type**: `boolean` (`true`, `false`, `1`, `0`)
- **Default**: `false`
- **Description**: Enable verbose output for all tasks
- **Config equivalent**: [`verbose`](./config.md#verbose)

### `TASK_SILENT`

- **Type**: `boolean` (`true`, `false`, `1`, `0`)
- **Default**: `false`
- **Description**: Disables echoing of commands
- **Config equivalent**: [`silent`](./config.md#silent)

### `TASK_COLOR`

- **Type**: `boolean` (`true`, `false`, `1`, `0`)
- **Default**: `true`
- **Description**: Enable colored output
- **Config equivalent**: [`color`](./config.md#color)

### `TASK_DISABLE_FUZZY`

- **Type**: `boolean` (`true`, `false`, `1`, `0`)
- **Default**: `false`
- **Description**: Disable fuzzy matching for task names
- **Config equivalent**: [`disable-fuzzy`](./config.md#disable-fuzzy)

### `TASK_CONCURRENCY`

- **Type**: `integer`
- **Description**: Limit number of tasks to run concurrently
- **Config equivalent**: [`concurrency`](./config.md#concurrency)

### `TASK_FAILFAST`

- **Type**: `boolean` (`true`, `false`, `1`, `0`)
- **Default**: `false`
- **Description**: When running tasks in parallel, stop all tasks if one fails
- **Config equivalent**: [`failfast`](./config.md#failfast)

### `TASK_DRY`

- **Type**: `boolean` (`true`, `false`, `1`, `0`)
- **Default**: `false`
- **Description**: Compiles and prints tasks in the order that they would be run, without executing them

### `TASK_ASSUME_YES`

- **Type**: `boolean` (`true`, `false`, `1`, `0`)
- **Default**: `false`
- **Description**: Assume "yes" as answer to all prompts

### `TASK_INTERACTIVE`

- **Type**: `boolean` (`true`, `false`, `1`, `0`)
- **Default**: `false`
- **Description**: Prompt for missing required variables

### `TASK_TEMP_DIR`

Defines the location of Task's temporary directory which is used for storing
checksums and temporary metadata. Can be relative like `tmp/task` or absolute
like `/tmp/.task` or `~/.task`. Relative paths are relative to the root
Taskfile, not the working directory. Defaults to: `./.task`.

### `TASK_CORE_UTILS`

This env controls whether the Bash interpreter will use its own
core utilities implemented in Go, or the ones available in the system.
Valid values are `true` (`1`) or `false` (`0`). By default, this is `true` on
Windows and `false` on other operating systems. We might consider making this
enabled by default on all platforms in the future.

### `FORCE_COLOR`

Force color output usage.

### Custom Colors

All color variables are [ANSI color codes][ansi]. You can specify multiple codes
separated by a semicolon. For example: `31;1` will make the text bold and red.
Task also supports 8-bit color (256 colors). You can specify these colors by
using the sequence `38;2;R:G:B` for foreground colors and `48;2;R:G:B` for
background colors where `R`, `G` and `B` should be replaced with values between
0 and 255.

For convenience, we allow foreground colors to be specified using shorthand,
comma-separated syntax: `R,G,B`. For example, `255,0,0` is equivalent to
`38;2;255:0:0`.

A table of variables and their defaults can be found below:

| ENV                         | Default |
| --------------------------- | ------- |
| `TASK_COLOR_RESET`          | `0`     |
| `TASK_COLOR_RED`            | `31`    |
| `TASK_COLOR_GREEN`          | `32`    |
| `TASK_COLOR_YELLOW`         | `33`    |
| `TASK_COLOR_BLUE`           | `34`    |

[ansi]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ANSI_escape_code

"""Task execution helpers."""
import os, re, subprocess, sys


def _subst(s, values):
    def repl(m):
        key=m.group(1)
        return str(values.get(key, os.environ.get(key, '')))
    s=re.sub(r'{{\s*\.([A-Za-z_][\w]*)\s*}}', repl, str(s))
    s=re.sub(r'{{\s*\.CLI_ARGS\s*}}', str(values.get('CLI_ARGS','')), s)
    return s


def run_tasks(config, names, *, cwd=None, dry=False, silent=False, force=False, cli_args='', cli_vars=None, exit_code=False):
    """Run task definitions from normalized Taskfile dictionary. Return exit status."""
    tasks=config.get('tasks') or {}
    cwd=cwd or os.getcwd()
    values=dict(config.get('vars') or {})
    values.update(cli_vars or {})
    values['CLI_ARGS']=cli_args
    active=set(); done=set()
    if not names: names=['default']
    def run(name):
        if name in done: return 0
        if name in active:
            print('task: Task called too many times (recursion limit)',file=sys.stderr); return 204
        task=tasks.get(name)
        if task is None:
            print(f'task: Task "{name}" does not exist',file=sys.stderr); return 200
        if isinstance(task,str): task={'cmds':[task]}
        elif isinstance(task,list): task={'cmds':task}
        task=task or {}; active.add(name)
        deps=task.get('deps', []) or []
        if isinstance(deps,str): deps=[deps]
        for dep in deps:
            if isinstance(dep,dict): dep=dep.get('task','')
            if dep and (rc:=run(str(dep))): active.remove(name); return rc
        for item in task.get('cmds',[]) or []:
            if isinstance(item,str): cmd=item; task_silent=False
            elif isinstance(item,dict):
                cmd=item.get('cmd',''); task_silent=item.get('silent',False)
            else: continue
            cmd=_subst(cmd,values)
            if not cmd: continue
            if not silent and not task.get('silent',False) and not task_silent:
                print(f'task: [{name}] {cmd}',flush=True)
            if not dry:
                proc=subprocess.run(cmd,shell=True,cwd=task.get('dir',cwd),env=os.environ.copy())
                if proc.returncode:
                    print(f'task: Failed to run task \"{name}\": exit status {proc.returncode}',file=sys.stderr)
                    active.remove(name); return proc.returncode if exit_code else 201
        active.remove(name); done.add(name); return 0
    for name in names:
        rc=run(name)
        if rc:return rc
    return 0
"""Implementation of Task's --init command."""
from pathlib import Path
import sys


TEMPLATE = '''# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://taskfile.dev/schema.json

version: '3'

vars:
  GREETING: Hello, world!

tasks:
  default:
    desc: Print a greeting message
    cmds:
      - echo "{{.GREETING}}"
    silent: true
'''


def run_init(directory='.'):
    """Create Taskfile.yml in directory. Return Task's process exit code."""
    path = Path(directory) / 'Taskfile.yml'
    if path.exists():
        print('task: A Taskfile already exists', file=sys.stderr)
        return 101
    try:
        path.write_text(TEMPLATE, encoding='utf-8')
    except OSError as e:
        print(f'task: {e}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print('Taskfile created: Taskfile.yml')
    return 0

const patch = "*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: /workspace/main.py
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+import os, sys, re, json, pathlib
+from execution import run_tasks
+from init_mode import run_init
+
+def scalar(s):
+    s=s.strip()
+    if not s:return {}
+    if s in ('true','True'): return True
+    if s in ('false','False'): return False
+    if s in ('null','~'): return None
+    if s.startswith(('"',"'")) and s[-1:]==s[0]: return s[1:-1]
+    if s.startswith('[') and s.endswith(']'):
+        return [scalar(x) for x in re.split(r',\s*(?![^\[]*\])',s[1:-1]) if x.strip()]
+    try:return int(s)
+    except:return s
+
+def parse_yaml(src):
+    # Small indentation-based YAML subset sufficient for ordinary Taskfiles.
+    lines=[]
+    for raw in src.splitlines():
+        if not raw.strip() or raw.lstrip().startswith('#'):continue
+        indent=len(raw)-len(raw.lstrip()); lines.append((indent,raw.strip()))
+    def block(i, indent):
+        islist= i<len(lines) and lines[i][1].startswith('- ')
+        out=[] if islist else {}
+        while i<len(lines) and lines[i][0]==indent:
+            txt=lines[i][1]
+            if islist:
+                if not txt.startswith('- '):break
+                item=txt[2:].strip(); i+=1
+                if ':' in item and not item.startswith(('"',"'")):
+                    k,v=item.split(':',1); obj={k.strip():scalar(v)}
+                    if i<len(lines) and lines[i][0]>indent:
+                        child,i=block(i,lines[i][0]); obj.update(child if isinstance(child,dict) else {})
+                    out.append(obj)
+                elif not item and i<len(lines) and lines[i][0]>indent:
+                    val,i=block(i,lines[i][0]); out.append(val)
+                else:out.append(scalar(item))
+            else:
+                if ':' not in txt: i+=1; continue
+                k,v=txt.split(':',1); k=k.strip(); v=v.strip(); i+=1
+                if v:out[k]=scalar(v)
+                elif i<len(lines) and lines[i][0]>indent:out[k],i=block(i,lines[i][0])
+                else:out[k]={}
+        return out,i
+    return block(0,lines[0][0])[0] if lines else {}
+
+def main(argv):
+    if '--version' in argv: print('3.51.1'); return 0
+    if '-h' in argv or '--help' in argv:
+        print('Usage: task [flags...] [task...]\n\nRuns the specified task(s). Falls back to the "default" task if no task name\nwas specified, or lists all tasks if an unknown task name was specified.\n\nOptions: --help --version --list --list-all --taskfile --dir --dry --silent --init')
+        return 0
+    if '--experiments' in argv:
+        print('* GENTLE_FORCE:     off\n* REMOTE_TASKFILES: off\n* ENV_PRECEDENCE:   off'); return 0
+    if '--completion' in argv:
+        try: shell=argv[argv.index('--completion')+1]
+        except: shell=''
+        if shell not in ('bash','zsh','fish','powershell'):
+            print('unknown shell: '+shell,file=sys.stderr); return 1
+        return 0
+    cwd=os.getcwd(); taskfile=''; dry='--dry' in argv or '-n' in argv; silent='--silent' in argv or '-s' in argv
+    init='--init' in argv or '-i' in argv
+    if '--dir' in argv:
+        try: cwd=os.path.abspath(argv[argv.index('--dir')+1])
+        except: pass
+    if '--taskfile' in argv or '-t' in argv:
+        key='--taskfile' if '--taskfile' in argv else '-t'
+        try: taskfile=argv[argv.index(key)+1]
+        except: pass
+    if init:return run_init(cwd)
+    if taskfile:
+        path=pathlib.Path(taskfile); path=path if path.is_absolute() else pathlib.Path(cwd)/path
+    else:
+        path=None
+        for d in [pathlib.Path(cwd),*pathlib.Path(cwd).parents]:
+            for n in ('Taskfile.yml','Taskfile.yaml','taskfile.yml','taskfile.yaml'):
+                p=d/n
+                if p.exists():path=p;break
+            if path:break
+    if not path or not path.exists():
+        loc=str(path) if taskfile else ''
+        print(f'task: No Taskfile found at "{loc}" (or any of the parent directories until ownership changed). Run `task --init` to create a new Taskfile.',file=sys.stderr); return 100
+    try: cfg=parse_yaml(path.read_text())
+    except Exception as e: print(f'task: {e}',file=sys.stderr); return 100
+    args=list(argv); names=[]; cli_args=''
+    if '--' in args: ix=args.index('--'); cli_args=' '.join(args[ix+1:]); args=args[:ix]
+    flags={'--list','-l','--list-all','-a','--json','-j','--dry','-n','--silent','-s','--verbose','-v','--force','-f','--parallel','-p','--status','--summary','-x','--exit-code','--disable-fuzzy','--color','-c','--no-status','--nested'}
+    valued={'--dir','-d','--taskfile','-t','--concurrency','-C','--output','-o','--sort'}
+    skip=False
+    for a in args:
+        if skip:skip=False;continue
+        if a in valued:skip=True;continue
+        if a in flags or a.startswith('--'):continue
+        names.append(a)
+    tasks=cfg.get('tasks') or {}
+    if '--list' in argv or '-l' in argv or '--list-all' in argv or '-a' in argv:
+        all_= '--list-all' in argv or '-a' in argv
+        entries=[(k,v if isinstance(v,dict) else {}) for k,v in tasks.items() if all_ or (isinstance(v,dict) and v.get('desc'))]
+        entries.sort(key=lambda p:p[0])
+        if '--json' in argv or '-j' in argv: print(json.dumps({'tasks':[{'name':k,'task':k,'desc':v.get('desc',''),'summary':v.get('summary',''),'aliases':v.get('aliases',[]),'up_to_date':False,'location':{'line':1,'column':3,'taskfile':str(path.resolve())}} for k,v in entries],'location':str(path.resolve())},indent=2))
+        elif silent:
+            for k,v in entries: print(k)
+        elif entries:
+            print('task: Available tasks for this project:')
+            for k,v in entries:print(f'* {k}:       {v.get("desc","")}')
+        else:print('task: No tasks with description available. Try --list-all to list all tasks')
+        return 0
+    # Strip option arguments before task names were collected.
+    return run_tasks(cfg,names,cwd=str(path.parent),dry=dry,silent=silent,force='--force' in argv or '-f' in argv,cli_args=cli_args,exit_code='--exit-code' in argv or '-x' in argv)
+
+if __name__=='__main__':sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
*** End Patch";

import os, sys, re, json, pathlib
from execution import run_tasks

from taskfile_discovery import find_taskfile
from config_mode import load_config
from info_mode import show_summary, check_status
from help_mode import show_help
from completion_mode import run_completion

def scalar(s):
    s=s.strip()
    if not s:return {}
    if s in ('true','True'): return True
    if s in ('false','False'): return False
    if s in ('null','~'): return None
    if s.startswith(('"',"'")) and s[-1:]==s[0]: return s[1:-1]
    if s.startswith('[') and s.endswith(']'):
        return [scalar(x) for x in re.split(r',\s*(?![^\[]*\])',s[1:-1]) if x.strip()]
    try:return int(s)
    except:return s

def parse_yaml(src):
    # Small indentation-based YAML subset sufficient for ordinary Taskfiles.
    lines=[]
    for raw in src.splitlines():
        if not raw.strip() or raw.lstrip().startswith('#'):continue
        indent=len(raw)-len(raw.lstrip()); lines.append((indent,raw.strip()))
    def block(i, indent):
        islist= i<len(lines) and lines[i][1].startswith('- ')

"""Load and namespace local Taskfile includes."""
from copy import deepcopy
from pathlib import Path
from taskfile_discovery import NAMES


def _locate(value, parent):
    p=Path(str(value)).expanduser()
    if not p.is_absolute(): p=Path(parent)/p
    if p.is_dir():
        for name in NAMES:
            candidate=p/name
            if candidate.is_file(): return candidate.resolve()
        return None
    return p.resolve() if p.is_file() else None


def _rewrite_refs(task, prefix):
    if not prefix:return
    for field in ('deps','cmds'):
        values=task.get(field) or []
        was_string=isinstance(values,str)
        if was_string: values=[values]
        rewritten=[]
        for item in values:
            if isinstance(item,dict):
                item=deepcopy(item)
                for key in ('task',):
                    if item.get(key) and ':' not in str(item[key]): item[key]=prefix+str(item[key])
            elif field=='deps' and isinstance(item,str) and ':' not in item:
                item=prefix+item
            rewritten.append(item)
        task[field]=rewritten[0] if was_string and len(rewritten)==1 else rewritten


def load_includes(config, root, parse_yaml):
    """Merge included task definitions into config using namespace prefixes."""
    config=deepcopy(config)
    main_root=Path(root).resolve()
    def merge(current, base, prefix='', inherited_vars=None, inherited_env=None, ancestry=None, excludes=None, root_level=False):
        ancestry=set(ancestry or ())
        current=deepcopy(current or {})
        tasks=current.get('tasks') or {}
        inherited_vars=dict(inherited_vars or {})
        inherited_vars.update(current.get('vars') or {})
        inherited_env=dict(inherited_env or {})
        inherited_env.update(current.get('env') or {})
        for name, definition in tasks.items():
            if str(name) in (excludes or []): continue
            d=deepcopy(definition if isinstance(definition,dict) else {'cmds':definition if isinstance(definition,list) else [definition]})
            olddir=d.get('dir')
            d['dir']=str((Path(base)/str(olddir)).resolve()) if olddir else str(Path(base).resolve())
            if not root_level and inherited_vars:
                d['vars']={**inherited_vars,**(d.get('vars') or {})}
            if not root_level and inherited_env:
                d['env']={**inherited_env,**(d.get('env') or {})}
            _rewrite_refs(d,prefix)
            if prefix and d.get('aliases'):
                aliases=d['aliases'] if isinstance(d['aliases'],list) else [d['aliases']]
                d['aliases']=[prefix+str(alias) for alias in aliases]
            tasks_key=prefix+str(name)
            out_tasks[tasks_key]=d
        for alias, spec in (current.get('includes') or {}).items():

## Include

Configuration for including external Taskfiles.

### `taskfile`

- **Type**: `string`
- **Required**: Yes
- **Description**: Path to the Taskfile or directory to include

```yaml
includes:
  backend: ./backend/Taskfile.yml
  # Shorthand for above
  frontend: ./frontend
```

### `dir`

- **Type**: `string`
- **Description**: Working directory for included tasks

```yaml
includes:
  api:
    taskfile: ./api
    dir: ./api
```

### `optional`

- **Type**: `bool`
- **Default**: `false`
- **Description**: Don't error if the included file doesn't exist

#### `if`

- **Type**: `string`
- **Description**: Shell command to conditionally execute the task. If the
  command exits with a non-zero code, the task is skipped (not failed).

```yaml
tasks:
  # Task only runs in CI environment
  deploy:
    if: '[ "$CI" = "true" ]'
    cmds:
      - ./deploy.sh

  # Using Go template expressions
  build-prod:
    if: '{{eq .ENV "production"}}'
    cmds:
      - go build -ldflags="-s -w" ./...
```

#### `dir`

- **Type**: `string`
- **Description**: The directory in which this task should run
- **Default**: If the task is in the root Taskfile, the default `dir` is
  `ROOT_DIR`. For included Taskfiles, the default `dir` is the value specified in
  their respective `includes.*.dir` field (if any).

```yaml
tasks:
  current-dir:
    dir: '{{.USER_WORKING_DIR}}'
    cmd: pwd
```

- **Type**: `Requires`
- **Description**: Required variables with optional enum validation

    for field in ('deps','cmds'):

        was_string=isinstance(values,str)
        if was_string: values=[values]
        rewritten=[]
        for item in values:

                item=deepcopy(item)
                for key in ('task',):

## Current progress

- The CLI implementation is integrated on the shared `main` branch. It includes task execution, listing and JSON output, YAML parsing, includes, help/version, completion, init, summary/status, and common error handling.
- I confirmed and fixed included-task context behavior. For an included task, `.TASKFILE` and `.TASKFILE_DIR` refer to its child Taskfile. Its working directory defaults to the root Taskfile directory, or to `includes.*.dir` when supplied. Both cases matched the reference in probes. This fix is pushed.
- I reviewed the newly added `requires.vars` and checksum behavior. The missing-variable case matched the reference exactly: exit code 206 and the same diagnostic.
- A checksum-cache mismatch remains under investigation. On the second run, the reference skipped the task and printed `task: Task "build" is up to date`; the implementation reran it. A teammate has since changed the checksum signature code on shared `main`, so that newer version needs to be tested before making another change.
- Recent `python3 -m py_compile *.py` runs passed before the current uncommitted checksum experiment.

## Current workspace state

- The local branch has uncommitted edits in `execution.py` from my checksum experiment.
- I fetched `team/main` at `f4726eb` after making those edits, but did not merge it. Its checksum implementation differs from the one I edited.
- Before continuing, inspect `git status` and `git diff`. The safest next step is to discard or reconcile my `execution.py` experiment, merge the fetched `team/main`, then rerun the checksum comparison.

## Next steps

1. Compare the fetched checksum implementation against the reference using fresh temporary directories. Run each implementation twice on a task with `sources` and `generates`; verify the second run skips.
2. If a mismatch remains, probe and fix it, then commit, fetch/merge `team/main`, and push with `git push team HEAD:main`.
3. Continue reviewing newly merged behavior and share concrete findings in `group`.

Useful fixture pattern: `sources: [src.txt]`, `generates: [out.txt]`, command `cp src.txt out.txt`. The reference stores cache data under `.task/checksum/build`; its second-run output was `task: Task "build" is up to date`.

## Constraints and preferences

- Reimplementation must use Python 3.10 and the standard library only. Observe the reference only through its normal CLI; do not inspect binaries, use the internet, or wrap the reference executable.
- Do not run `/workspace/compile.sh`.
- The user explicitly directed continued tool use, whole-program review, reference comparisons, fixes, and pushes. Do not stop after a status response.

p='execution.py';s=open(p).read().replace('import os, subprocess, sys, shlex, glob, hashlib, json','import os, subprocess, sys, shlex, glob, hashlib, json')
a=s.index('def _file_signature(');b=s.index('\n\ndef run_tasks',a)
s=s[:a]+'''def _file_signature(task, task_dir, root, name):
    sources=_patterns(task.get('sources'))
    generates=_patterns(task.get('generates'))
    if not sources:return None
    # Task uses a deterministic checksum over the task definition and source files.
    records=[]
    for pattern in sources:
        paths=glob.glob(os.path.join(task_dir,pattern),recursive=True)
        if not paths: records.append(pattern); continue
        for path in sorted(paths):
            try:
                st=os.stat(path)
                records.extend((os.path.relpath(path,root),str(st.st_size),str(st.st_mtime_ns)))
            except OSError: records.append(path)
    payload=json.dumps([task,records,[(p,sorted(glob.glob(os.path.join(task_dir,p),recursive=True))) for p in generates]],sort_keys=True,default=str,separators=(',',':'))
    return hashlib.md5(payload.encode()).hexdigest()
''' +s[b:]
open(p,'w').write(s)
PY

"""Implementation of Task's --init command."""
from pathlib import Path
import sys


TEMPLATE = '''# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://taskfile.dev/schema.json

version: '3'

vars:
  GREETING: Hello, world!

tasks:
  default:
    desc: Print a greeting message
    cmds:
      - echo "{{.GREETING}}"
    silent: true
'''


def run_init(directory='.', filename='Taskfile.yml'):
    """Create a Taskfile at filename. Return Task's process exit code."""
    path = Path(filename)
    if not path.is_absolute(): path = Path(directory) / path
    display = str(Path(filename))
    existing = (
        'Taskfile.yml', 'Taskfile.yaml', 'taskfile.yml', 'taskfile.yaml',
        'Taskfile.dist.yml', 'Taskfile.dist.yaml',
        'taskfile.dist.yml', 'taskfile.dist.yaml',
    )
    if path.exists() or (display == 'Taskfile.yml' and any((Path(directory) / name).exists() for name in existing)):
        print('task: A Taskfile already exists', file=sys.stderr)
        return 101
    try:
        path.write_text(TEMPLATE, encoding='utf-8')
    except OSError as e:
        print(f'task: {e}', file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(f'Taskfile created: {display}')
    return 0

"""Load and namespace local Taskfile includes."""
from copy import deepcopy
from pathlib import Path
import re
from taskfile_discovery import NAMES


class IncludeError(Exception):
    pass


class IncludeParseError(Exception):
    def __init__(self, path, message):
        self.path=path
        self.message=message


def _locate(value, parent):
    p=Path(str(value)).expanduser()
    if not p.is_absolute(): p=Path(parent)/p
    if p.is_dir():
        for name in NAMES:
            candidate=p/name
            if candidate.is_file(): return candidate.resolve()
        return None
    return p.resolve() if p.is_file() else None


def _rewrite_refs(task, prefix):
    if not prefix:return
    for field in ('deps','cmds'):
        values=task.get(field) or []
        was_string=isinstance(values,str)
        if was_string: values=[values]
        rewritten=[]
        for item in values:
            if isinstance(item,dict):
                item=deepcopy(item)
                for key in ('task',):
                    if item.get(key) and ':' not in str(item[key]): item[key]=prefix+str(item[key])
            elif field=='deps' and isinstance(item,str) and ':' not in item:
                item=prefix+item
            rewritten.append(item)
        task[field]=rewritten[0] if was_string and len(rewritten)==1 else rewritten


def load_includes(config, root, parse_yaml, root_taskfile=None):
    """Merge included task definitions into config using namespace prefixes."""
    config=deepcopy(config)
    main_root=Path(root).resolve()
    def merge(current, base, prefix='', inherited_vars=None, inherited_env=None, ancestry=None, excludes=None, root_level=False, include_aliases=None, source_file=None, default_task_dir=None):
        ancestry=set(ancestry or ())
        current=deepcopy(current or {})
        tasks=current.get('tasks') or {}
        inherited_vars=dict(inherited_vars or {})
        inherited_vars.update(current.get('vars') or {})
        inherited_env=dict(inherited_env or {})
        inherited_env.update(current.get('env') or {})
        for name, definition in tasks.items():
            if str(name) in (excludes or []): continue
            d=deepcopy(definition if isinstance(definition,dict) else {'cmds':definition if isinstance(definition,list) else [definition]})
            if not root_level and source_file:
                d['_taskfile']=str(Path(source_file).resolve())
                d['_source_task_name']=str(name)
            d['_TASKFILE']=str(Path(source_file).resolve()) if source_file else ''
            d['_TASKFILE_DIR']=str(Path(source_file).resolve().parent) if source_file else str(Path(base).resolve())
            olddir=d.get('dir')
            task_base=Path(default_task_dir or main_root)
            d['dir']=str((task_base/str(olddir)).resolve()) if olddir else str(task_base.resolve())
            if not root_level and inherited_vars:
                d['vars']={**inherited_vars,**(d.get('vars') or {})}
            if not root_level and inherited_env:
                d['env']={**inherited_env,**(d.get('env') or {})}
            _rewrite_refs(d,prefix)
            aliases=d.get('aliases',[]) or []
            if isinstance(aliases,str): aliases=[aliases]
            if prefix:
                aliases=[prefix+str(alias) for alias in aliases]
            aliases.extend(str(alias_prefix)+str(name) for alias_prefix in (include_aliases or []))
            if aliases: d['aliases']=aliases
            if source_file:
                d['_source_taskfile']=str(source_file)
                try:
                    for line_no, raw in enumerate(Path(source_file).read_text(encoding='utf-8').splitlines(),1):
                        prefix_text='  '+str(name)+':'
                        if raw.startswith(prefix_text) and (len(raw)==len(prefix_text) or raw[len(prefix_text)].isspace()):
                            d['_source_line']=line_no
                            break
                except OSError:
                    pass
            tasks_key=prefix+str(name)
            out_tasks[tasks_key]=d
        for alias, spec in (current.get('includes') or {}).items():
            opts=spec if isinstance(spec,dict) else {'taskfile':spec}
            requested=Path(str(opts.get('taskfile',''))).expanduser()
            if not requested.is_absolute(): requested=Path(base)/requested
            target=_locate(opts.get('taskfile',''),base)
            if not target:
                if opts.get('optional'): continue
                raise IncludeError(str(requested.resolve()))
            target_s=str(target)
            if target_s in ancestry: continue
            try:
                source=target.read_text(encoding='utf-8')
                child=parse_yaml(source)
            except (OSError,ValueError) as e:
                display=str(target.relative_to(main_root)) if target.is_relative_to(main_root) else str(target)
                raise IncludeParseError(display,str(e))
            if not isinstance(child,dict) or (child.get('tasks') is not None and not isinstance(child.get('tasks'),dict)):
                display=str(target.relative_to(main_root)) if target.is_relative_to(main_root) else str(target)
                badline=next((i for i,line in enumerate(source.splitlines(),1) if re.search(r':\s*\[\s*$',line)),1)
                raise IncludeParseError(display,f'yaml: line {badline}: did not find expected node content')
            flat=bool(opts.get('flatten',False))
            child_prefix=prefix+(str(alias)+':' if not flat else '')
            child_vars=dict(opts.get('vars') or {})
            child_vars.update(inherited_vars)
            child_env=dict(inherited_env)
            child_env.update(opts.get('env') or {})
            # Included task files execute from the root Taskfile directory by
            # default; an include-level `dir` explicitly changes that base.
            child_base=Path(opts.get('dir') or main_root)
            if not child_base.is_absolute(): child_base=Path(base)/child_base
            extra_aliases=opts.get('aliases',[]) or []
            if isinstance(extra_aliases,str): extra_aliases=[extra_aliases]
            alias_prefixes=[prefix+(str(a)+':') for a in extra_aliases] if not flat else []
            task_dir=Path(opts.get('dir') or default_task_dir or main_root)
            if not task_dir.is_absolute(): task_dir=Path(base)/task_dir
            merge(child,child_base,child_prefix,child_vars,child_env,ancestry | {target_s},opts.get('excludes'),include_aliases=alias_prefixes,source_file=target,default_task_dir=task_dir)
    out_tasks={}
    merge(config,main_root,root_level=True,source_file=root_taskfile,default_task_dir=main_root)
    config['tasks']=out_tasks
    return config

        return 1

    taskfile_value=next((a.split('=',1)[1] for a in argv if a.startswith('--taskfile=')),None)

            if arg in value_flags:

            if arg in ('--init','-i') or arg.startswith('-') or arg.startswith('--'):

def check_status(config, name, cwd=None, taskfile=None):
    """Return success only when status commands all report the task current."""
    _, task = _lookup_task(config, name)
    if task is None:
        print(f'task: Task "{name}" does not exist', file=sys.stderr)
        return 200
    task = task if isinstance(task, dict) else {}
    checks = task.get("status") or []
    if isinstance(checks, str):
        checks = [checks]
    root = os.path.abspath(cwd or os.getcwd())
    taskfile_dir=task.get("_TASKFILE_DIR") or root
    taskfile_path=task.get("_TASKFILE") or (os.path.abspath(taskfile) if taskfile and taskfile != "stdin" else "stdin")
    values = resolve_vars(config.get("vars") or {}, env=os.environ)
    values.update(task.get("vars") or {})
    task_dir=task.get("dir") or root
    if not os.path.isabs(task_dir): task_dir=os.path.join(root,task_dir)
    values.update({"TASK":name,"ALIAS":name,"ROOT_DIR":root,"TASKFILE_DIR":taskfile_dir,
                   "TASKFILE":taskfile_path,"ROOT_TASKFILE":os.path.abspath(taskfile) if taskfile and taskfile != "stdin" else "stdin",
                   "TASK_DIR":os.path.abspath(task_dir), "FILE_PATH_SEPARATOR":os.sep})
    task_dir = values["TASK_DIR"]
    env = os.environ.copy()
    for key, value in values.items():
        if isinstance(value,dict): continue
        env[str(key)] = str(value)
    current=True
    validated=False
    for check in checks:
        validated=True
        try:
            if isinstance(check, dict): check=check.get("sh") or check.get("cmd") or ""
            check=_template(check,values)
            if subprocess.run(str(check), shell=True, cwd=task_dir, env=env,
                              stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL).returncode:
                current=False; break
        except OSError:
            current=False; break
    sources=_patterns(task.get("sources"))
    generates=_patterns(task.get("generates"))
    method=task.get("method",config.get("method","checksum"))
    if sources and generates and method!='none':
        validated=True
        temp_dir=os.environ.get('TASK_TEMP_DIR','.task')
        if not os.path.isabs(temp_dir): temp_dir=os.path.join(root,temp_dir)
        cache_file=os.path.join(temp_dir,'checksum',str(name))
        all_sources=all(glob.glob(os.path.join(task_dir,p),recursive=True) for p in sources)
        all_generates=all(glob.glob(os.path.join(task_dir,p),recursive=True) for p in generates)
        try:
            saved=open(cache_file,encoding='utf-8').read().strip()
            signature=_file_signature(task,task_dir,root,name)
            if not (all_sources and all_generates and saved==signature): current=False

            current=False
    if current and validated:return 0
